headline: Geopolitical Fog Keeps Buyers Cautious as Consumer Names Crumble
body_html:
Thursday's session ended without conviction, as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a margin of roughly 345 to 202 across the tracked universe. The dominant theme was uncertainty: investors parsed competing signals from the Strait of Hormuz, where an Iranian parliamentary committee reviewed a draft bill to restrict passage for American and Israeli vessels, even as separate diplomatic back-channels kept hopes of a resolution flickering. The S&P 500 drifted little changed on the day, underscoring the market's reluctance to take a strong directional stance.

Sector rotation told a clear story. Energy and semiconductors were the lone bright spots, posting gains of 0.66% and 0.53% respectively, while consumer-facing names absorbed the heaviest punishment, falling 2.64% as a group. Homebuilders were nearly as bruised, off 2.40%. Software and industrials also retreated, suggesting that any appetite for risk was tightly concentrated rather than broadly distributed.

The session's standout mover to the downside was Universal Technical Institute, which shed more than 34% — a sharp reminder that earnings-driven air pockets can dwarf whatever the macro tape is doing. On the flip side, Diodes surged 15.34%, lending further credibility to the quiet resilience building in semiconductor supply-chain names.

briefs.headline: LegalZoom Plunges 30% After Results Disappoint
briefs.body: LegalZoom.com fell 30.06% in one of the session's most punishing single-stock moves. The tech-legal-services platform appeared unable to satisfy investor expectations, extending a broader pattern of pain in software and internet-services names that have struggled to justify elevated valuations in the current rate environment.

briefs.headline: Datadog Drops Sharply as Software Sentiment Sours
briefs.body: Observability-software provider Datadog slid 19.03%, dragging the broader software sector lower. The decline reinforced Thursday's rotation away from high-multiple technology, with the software group finishing down 0.74% overall even as semiconductor peers held in positive territory.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Passage Proposal Faces Industry Pushback
briefs.body: A draft Iranian bill to bar vessels deemed hostile from the Strait of Hormuz drew skepticism from shipping-industry sources, who described the proposal as unworkable in practice. Oil prices edged higher on the headline risk, helping lift the energy sector to the top of Thursday's sector leaderboard.

briefs.headline: European Equities Extend Record Run on Earnings and Iran Diplomacy
briefs.body: Across the Atlantic, European shares stretched their streak of all-time highs, buoyed by solid corporate earnings and cautious optimism that US-Iran tensions could de-escalate. The divergence between European and domestic sentiment highlighted how geopolitical hopes were being priced differently across regions.

briefs.headline: Encompass Health Jumps 12% on Strong Results
briefs.body: Encompass Health posted a 12.36% gain, standing out as a rare bright spot in a healthcare sector that finished essentially flat on the day, down just 0.06%. The rehabilitation-facilities operator's move suggested investors are willing to reward companies that deliver clear earnings beats even in a risk-averse tape.

briefs.headline: American Airlines Trims Elite Perks on Domestic Routes
briefs.body: American Airlines announced it would end complimentary business-class upgrades for elite frequent flyers on long domestic itineraries, a policy shift that signals continued pressure on airline cost structures. The move is likely to test loyalty among the carrier's most valuable customers heading into a seasonally important travel period.
